title: NVision Quantum Technologies Expands into Molecular Quantum Computing with Photonic Integrated Architecture - Quantum Computing Report
gist: NVision Quantum Technologies, a German company with 20 commercial Polaris hyperpolarized-MRI systems deployed, is expanding into quantum computing via PIQC, a room-temperature molecular qubit architecture built on silicon photonic chips with OLED-like thin-film fabrication. The move is backed by a $55M Series B led by Abbott and the EIB plus EU and German public projects.

themes.theme: NVision pivot from MRI to molecular quantum computing

insights.claim: NVision Quantum Technologies is expanding from its commercial hyperpolarized MRI platform into quantum computing hardware through its PIQC (Photonic Integrated Quantum Chip) molecular architecture, as described by CEO Sella Brosh.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: A revenue-generating quantum sensing company is entering the qubit hardware race, giving it a commercial base few QC startups have.
insights.locator: In a technical briefing and podcast

insights.claim: NVision is applying the same quantum spin principles and proprietary synthetic organic chemistry platform used for MRI hyperpolarization to fabricate optically addressable molecular-scale qubits, called Pixie, integrated directly into silicon photonic circuits.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Shared chemistry and spin know-how across sensing and computing could lower R&D cost and de-risk the pivot.
insights.quote: NVision is now applying these same quantum spin principles to fabricate optically addressable, molecular-scale qubits (termed Pixie) directly integrated into silicon photonic circuits.

insights.claim: NVision's PIQC molecular qubit approach aims to bypass the monolithic physical constraints of superconducting and ion-trap quantum computers by combining long coherence, room-temperature optical control and direct single-photon emission.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: If room-temperature molecular qubits work, they challenge the cryogenic and trapped-ion incumbents' cost and scaling assumptions.
insights.quote: The PIQC strategy bypasses the monolithic physical constraints of traditional superconducting and ion-trap architectures by combining long coherence, room-temperature optical control, and direct single-photon emission.

insights.claim: NVision plans to deposit roughly 100 nm thin films of synthetic organic molecules into optical cavities of silicon photonic chips using techniques analogous to commercial OLED display manufacturing, aiming for a scalable photonically-entangled gate architecture for fault-tolerant quantum computing.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Borrowing mature OLED-style fabrication could make qubit manufacturing cheaper and more scalable, though fault tolerance remains an aspiration.

insights.claim: NVision's interconnect design is a modular photonic-entangled gate architecture that connects distinct molecular qubit sites via photons.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Modular photonic networking is a key route to scaling beyond single-chip limits.
insights.locator: NVision Commercial Deployment & Hardware Architectural Profile

insights.claim: NVision's Polaris system hyperpolarizes nuclear spins of organic sugar molecules, boosting MRI signal levels by nearly 100,000x for early cancer detection and rapid metabolic therapy assessment.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: A concrete quantum-sensing product with clinical use cases supports revenue and validates the company's spin-engineering core.
insights.quote: boosting MRI signal levels by nearly 100,000x for early cancer detection and rapid metabolic therapy assessment

insights.claim: NVision has 20 Polaris systems deployed across Asia, Europe and North America, including at MSK, UCSF, Penn Medicine and WashU, with onsite clinical preparation not requiring specialized physics staff.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: An installed base at leading cancer centers signals real commercial adoption of quantum sensing.
insights.quote: 20 systems deployed across Asia, Europe, and North America (e.g., MSK, UCSF, Penn Medicine, WashU)
insights.locator: NVision Commercial Deployment & Hardware Architectural Profile

insights.claim: Through the EUR 8.3 million EU-funded Q-AID initiative, NVision deployed the first two Polaris systems at IBEC in Barcelona and the University of Antwerp for quantum-enhanced metabolic MRI and AI-powered oncology diagnostics, and completed another deployment at UCLouvain in Belgium.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Public-funded European deployments extend NVision's footprint and pair quantum sensing with AI diagnostics.

insights.claim: Germany's Federal Ministry of Research extended the QuE-MRT lighthouse project involving NVision through August 2028, expanding total project volume to about EUR 20 million.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Multi-year German government backing provides non-dilutive funding visibility through 2028.
insights.quote: Germany’s Federal Ministry of Research extended the QuE-MRT lighthouse project through August 2028, expanding the total project volume to ~€20 million.

insights.claim: NVision's quantum computing expansion complements its $55 million Series B led by Abbott and the EIB and builds on its selection by EuroHPC JU for the QOSMOS molecular spin-qubit project.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Backing from a major medtech strategic (Abbott) and EU institutions signals credibility and capital for both business lines.
insights.quote: NVision’s $55 million Series B financing round led by Abbott and the EIB

insights.claim: NVision also has a clinical sensing footprint at the University of Cambridge and Aarhus University's EUR 5.4M MIRAQLE research hub.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Academic partnerships widen the research pipeline feeding both sensing and qubit efforts.
